project.name: zombie_apocalypse
project.description: A Godot 4 based 2D side-scrolling zombie apocalypse game with 6 playable characters, zombie/saw enemies, collectible items, and modular scene architecture.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Primary project documentation for the Zombie Apocalypse Godot 4 game. Covers characters, enemies, items, levels, controls, testing with GUT, architecture layout, and CI/CD pipeline.

nodes.name: 2D Side-Scrolling Zombie Apocalypse
nodes.summary: The core game genre: a 2D side-scroller built with Godot 4 featuring playable characters, zombie and saw enemies, collectible items, and modular scene-based architecture.

nodes.name: Playable Character Roster
nodes.summary: Six playable characters: Female Ninja (shuriken, fast), Male Ninja (shuriken, balanced), Male Robot (machine gun, heavy), Female Ranger (bow, agile), Male Ranger (bow, balanced), Dino (stomp, double-jump).

nodes.name: Enemy Types
nodes.summary: Three enemy/obstacle types: Zombie (standard melee), Saw (spinning blade obstacle), Barrier (impassable wall segment).

nodes.name: Collectible Items
nodes.summary: Three collectible item types: Health (restores HP), Energy Stone (fills stamina bar), Ammo (replenishes ammunition).

nodes.name: Project Architecture
nodes.summary: Modular directory layout: scripts/ for GDScript logic, scenes/ for .tscn files, resources/ for .tres files, tests/ for GUT unit tests, docs/add/ for Architecture Decision Documents.

nodes.name: CI/CD Pipeline
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions pipeline running gdlint for GDScript linting, GUT automated unit tests, and lint-paths for file/folder naming convention checks.

nodes.name: Generic behaviour script pattern
nodes.summary: An inheritance-based architecture where reusable generic scripts hold shared gameplay logic and character-specific scripts override only specialised behaviour.

nodes.name: Version History
nodes.summary: Project versioned from 1.0.0 (initial characters) through 1.1.0 (generic behaviours), 1.2.0 (ranger + base class refactor), and 1.3.0 (Dino character). Follows semver and Keep a Changelog conventions.

nodes.name: AI Tooling Integration
nodes.summary: Repository integrates multiple AI/code-graph tools: understand-anything (knowledge graph), codegraph (symbol lookup), graphify (file graph). AGENTS.md defines a prioritized workflow for AI agents navigating the codebase.

nodes.name: Architecture Decision Documents Index
nodes.summary: Index of accepted Architecture Decision Documents for the Zombie Apocalypse project, linking the migration, behaviour architecture, multi-character design, and testing decisions.

nodes.name: ADD-001: Godot 4 Migration
nodes.summary: Records the decision to fully migrate the project from Godot 3 to Godot 4, including API, node, scene, and GDScript changes required by the new engine version.

nodes.name: ADD-002: Generic Behaviour Scripts Architecture
nodes.summary: Defines the inheritance-based architecture of generic base scripts that centralise shared movement, combat, projectile, level, and tween behaviour for characters and scenes.

nodes.name: ADD-003: Multi-Character World Scene Design
nodes.summary: Describes the top-level World_Scene architecture for instantiating multiple playable characters, switching between them at runtime, and sharing HUD and level state.

nodes.name: ADD-004: GUT Testing Framework Choice
nodes.summary: Captures the decision to use the GUT framework for Godot-native automated testing, including headless CLI execution and GitHub Actions integration.

nodes.name: Godot 4 migration
nodes.summary: A full-engine migration strategy that updates scripts, scenes, node types, signal patterns, and tooling to Godot 4.x and GDScript 2.0 conventions.

nodes.name: Multi-character world scene design
nodes.summary: A scene orchestration model where World_Scene owns the roster of playable characters, controls active-character switching, preserves level state, and updates shared UI.

nodes.name: GUT testing approach
nodes.summary: A Godot-native automated testing strategy using GUT for unit tests, headless execution, and CI verification of gameplay scripts.

nodes.name: generic_character_behaviour.gd
nodes.summary: Base class for all playable characters. Extends CharacterBody2D and provides gravity, movement, jumping, damage, invincibility, blood/flicker effects, bullet shooting, collision areas, and death/respawn signal logic.

nodes.name: generic_bullet_behaviour.gd
nodes.summary: Base class for all bullets. Handles movement, animation, collision with bricks and enemy characters, damage formula (base + 5*power), and despawn on non-brick surface hits.

nodes.name: generic_tween_script.gd
nodes.summary: Reusable tween script for moving scene objects (platforms, obstacles) back and forth along X/Y axes. Configurable via exports for direction, distance, and duration.

nodes.name: generic_level_script.gd
nodes.summary: Minimal base script for level scenes extending Node2D. Emits level_entered on _ready and level_exited on _exit_tree.

nodes.name: ranger.gd
nodes.summary: Ranger character script extending generic_character_behaviour. Female ranger with shoot, melee, and slide actions. Uses 'run' instead of 'walk' animation name.

nodes.name: dino.gd
nodes.summary: Dino character extending generic_character_behaviour. Features a stomp instant-kill mechanic on falling, tail-swipe melee, no projectile or slide. Animation names use dino_ prefix without gender.

nodes.name: World Scene
nodes.summary: Main world/controller scene. It tracks active level state, instantiates playable characters, supports tab-based character switching, advances levels, resets characters, and renders the HUD in a CanvasLayer.

nodes.name: project.godot
nodes.summary: Main Godot project settings file. It sets Zombie Apocalypse as the app name, points startup to scenes/World_Scene.tscn, and defines core input mappings for movement, combat, respawn, and character switching.

nodes.name: GitHub Actions tests workflow
nodes.summary: CI workflow referenced by the testing ADD as the automation that runs the GUT suite for GDScript and tests changes.

nodes.name: GUT addon
nodes.summary: Vendored Godot Unit Test framework dependency used to run project tests inside the Godot runtime and editor.

nodes.name: test_character_behaviour.gd
nodes.summary: GUT test suite for generic_character_behaviour.gd. Covers _shoot_bullet guards, _take_damage (health/energy/invincibility), invincibility timer, and _apply_incoming_damage scenarios.

nodes.name: test_bullet_behaviour.gd
nodes.summary: GUT test suite for generic_bullet_behaviour.gd. Tests _set_speed velocity formula, non-brick hit count despawn threshold, damage+power formula, and _get_scale_for_power outputs.

nodes.name: test_tween_script.gd
nodes.summary: GUT test suite for generic_tween_script.gd. Tests direction toggling, zero-direction no-op, _set_initial_movement position calculation, and _on_tween_completed state reset.

nodes.name: test_adventure_girl.gd
nodes.summary: GUT integration test for the AdventureGirl character scene. Instantiates the full scene and verifies type/gender, absence of jump_shoot/jump_melee animations, and presence of run animation.

nodes.name: download_gut.sh
nodes.summary: Idempotent shell script that downloads the Godot 4.3-stable headless binary for running GUT tests locally. Detects OS and architecture (Linux x86_64/arm64, macOS universal, Windows x86_64), downloads the correct build from the official Godot GitHub releases page, installs it to ./bin/godot, makes it executable, and prints the absolute path. Skips download if binary already exists.

nodes.name: run_gut_tests.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that runs GUT (Godot Unit Test) tests using the Godot headless binary. Delegates binary acquisition to download_gut.sh, then invokes Godot headless with gut_cmdln.gd pointing at res://tests/ and exits after completion. Entry point for test execution.

nodes.name: verify.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that verifies the project structure by checking that all required GDScript files exist: generic_character_behaviour.gd, generic_bullet_behaviour.gd, generic_tween_script.gd, generic_level_script.gd, ranger.gd, and dino.gd. Exits with error if any are missing.

nodes.name: GUT Testing Infrastructure
nodes.summary: The testing infrastructure built around the GUT (Godot Unit Test) addon. Comprises the headless Godot binary, the gut_cmdln.gd command-line runner, and test files under res://tests/. Orchestrated by download_gut.sh and run_gut_tests.sh to enable automated and local test execution.

nodes.name: Project Structure Verification
nodes.summary: The process of asserting that all required GDScript source files are present in the repository before builds or tests proceed. Implemented by verify.sh and acts as a sanity-check gate for CI pipelines.

nodes.name: Godot Headless Binary
nodes.summary: The Godot 4.3-stable server/headless executable used to run GUT tests without a display. Downloaded from official Godot GitHub releases and cached at bin/godot. Required by run_gut_tests.sh to execute tests in CI or local environments.

nodes.name: GenericCharacterBehaviour
nodes.summary: Base character class extending CharacterBody2D. Manages health/energy/ammo stats, movement speed, jump count, timers (death, invincibility, daze, glide), attack areas, and signals for HUD refresh and level reload.

nodes.name: _start_process
nodes.summary: Main per-frame driver: calls _animate_player, then resolves X and Y axis collisions separately via move_and_collide, and triggers pit-death respawn if position.y exceeds PIT_DEATH_THRESHOLD.

nodes.name: _take_damage
nodes.summary: Applies damage to the character. Energy acts as a shield — damage drains energy first; overflow spills into health. Sets blood flag and marks shield_indicator when energy depletes.

nodes.name: _shoot_bullet
nodes.summary: Instantiates bullet_scene, sets power/damage/direction based on sprite flip, decrements ammo, and adds bullet to the scene tree. Guards against null bullet_scene or zero ammo.

nodes.name: _handle_timers
nodes.summary: Orchestrates all per-frame timer ticks: glide, daze, blood/particle, and invincibility (including flicker and death state handling).

nodes.name: _emit_reload
nodes.summary: On death: emits reload signal for main characters (triggers level reload), or drops a Bone_Scene pickup and frees the enemy node.

nodes.name: GenericBulletBehaviour
nodes.summary: Base bullet class extending CharacterBody2D. Tracks movement direction, speed, power level, and damage. Uses cached Area2D and CollisionShape2D nodes for efficient collision checks.

nodes.name: _animate_bullet
nodes.summary: Per-frame bullet update: increments delta_time, sets speed, plays animation, applies power-based scale, moves via move_and_collide, checks overlapping bodies, and handles brick/non-brick despawn logic.

nodes.name: _check_collision_objects
nodes.summary: Checks Area2D overlapping bodies for enemy_character group members, disables collision shape, deals damage scaled by power, then frees the bullet.

nodes.name: _get_scale_for_power
nodes.summary: Pure helper returning the Vector2 scale constant corresponding to bullet power level 0, 1, or 2.

nodes.name: GenericLevelScript
nodes.summary: Base level class. Declares level_entered and level_exited signals and emits them on node lifecycle events.

nodes.name: GenericTweenScript
nodes.summary: Tween helper class for Node2D objects. Runs a linear/ease-in-out tween to a target position and reverses direction on completion for ping-pong motion.

nodes.name: _start_tween_process
nodes.summary: Starts a Godot 4 Tween to animate position to movement_position over tween_duration, connecting _on_tween_completed. Guards against re-entry with tween_running flag.

nodes.name: _on_tween_completed
nodes.summary: Callback fired when a tween finishes. Reverses X and Y directions, computes the next movement_position, and resets tween_running for the next cycle.

nodes.name: Ranger
nodes.summary: Ranger character: female type, supports shoot (action_1), melee (action_2), slide (action_3), and double-jump. Overrides _reset_character_sprite_states to use 'run' animation.

nodes.name: _ready
nodes.summary: Initializes ranger: sets type/gender, gets AnimatedSprite, sets up collisions, preloads ninja bullet scene, emits character_ready signal, and subscribes to saw signals.

nodes.name: control_character
nodes.summary: Handles all player input for the ranger: shoot, melee, slide, jump, move left/right, and respawn. Called from _physics_process each frame.

nodes.name: _physics_process
nodes.summary: Physics update: runs area collision checks, then control_character input handling, then base _start_process for movement/gravity.

nodes.name: Dino
nodes.summary: Dino character with stomp (instant-kill on landing), tail-swipe melee, jump, and run. Overrides _change_sprite_animation to use dino_ prefix. No shoot or slide.

nodes.name: _check_stomp
nodes.summary: Checks if the dino is falling fast enough (>= STOMP_MIN_VELOCITY) and has enemies under StompArea2D. Deals instant-kill damage, dazes them, grants a bounce, and prevents multi-stomp per jump.

nodes.name: _handle_input
nodes.summary: Reads player input for dino: move left/right, jump (single), and tail-swipe (action_2). Sets animation states and activates melee hitbox.

nodes.name: _physics_process
nodes.summary: Physics update: calls _handle_input, _check_stomp (before landing resets velocity), then super._start_process and area checks, then sprite state reset.

nodes.name: TestCharacterBehaviour
nodes.summary: GUT test class with before_each/after_each lifecycle. Tests damage, invincibility, blood flag, and incoming damage routing through action1/2/3 for GenericCharacterBehaviour.

nodes.name: TestBulletBehaviour

nodes.name: TestTweenScript

nodes.name: TestAdventureGirl

tour.title: Project overview and entrypoint
tour.description: Start with the high-level docs to learn what the game is, which characters and enemies exist, and how the repository is organized. Then open the Godot project settings to see the real runtime entrypoint and the input map that the rest of the code assumes.

tour.title: Architecture decisions and design intent
tour.description: Before diving into scripts, read the ADD index and the accepted decisions so you understand why the project is structured this way. These documents explain the Godot 4 migration, the generic-behaviour inheritance model, the multi-character World_Scene design, and the choice of GUT for testing.

tour.title: Core gameplay foundation
tour.description: Next, read the shared gameplay scripts because they define the reusable rules that most other scenes and character scripts build on. The character base handles movement, damage, invincibility, signals, and shooting, while the bullet, tween, and level scripts cover the common projectile, moving-platform, and level lifecycle behavior.

tour.title: Character specializations
tour.description: Once the base class is clear, compare the specialised playable characters to see how the inheritance model is actually used. Ranger shows a fairly standard projectile-based extension, while Dino demonstrates a more distinct melee-heavy variant with stomp and custom input/physics behavior, and each has a matching scene setup.

tour.title: World orchestration, enemies, and levels
tour.description: After understanding individual characters, move up to the scene layer where the game is assembled. World_Scene controls active-character switching and shared HUD/state, while the enemy and level scenes show how hazards, progression, and combat spaces are composed into the actual playable game.

tour.title: CI/CD and developer automation
tour.description: Once you know the code layout, read the automation that protects it. The GitHub Actions workflows show the quality gates in CI, and the shell scripts explain how local verification and headless Godot test execution are expected to work on a developer machine.

tour.title: Tests as executable documentation
tour.description: Finish by reading the test suite, because it confirms the intended behavior of the most important systems in executable form. The tests make the contracts around character damage/shooting, bullet math, tween state changes, and a real character scene much easier to understand than implementation code alone.
